interest: Index on a 1934 US-Japan joint radio broadcast's protocol issues.
overview: Docket (1934): a planned US-Japan radio broadcast lost its Secretary-of-State speaker after Japan's Foreign Minister withdrew, substituting a private figure.

people.name: Henry W. Taft
people.role: President of the Japan Society of New York

people.name: William R. Castle
people.role: Former Under Secretary of State / diplomat connected with Japanese affairs

subfiles.about: Informs the State Department of a planned July 4th international broadcast arranged with the Japanese Broadcasting Company and requests a State Department speaker.
subfiles.summary: NBC asks State for a speaker on a July 4th US-Japan broadcast also featuring Japan's Foreign Minister and Ambassador Grew.
subfiles.title: NBC Request for State Department Speaker for July 4th Broadcast
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE: PC), Department of State

subfiles.about: Discusses NBC's request for Secretary of State Cordell Hull to deliver a talk for the July 4th international radio broadcast.
subfiles.from: James Clement Dunn, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Dunn weighs whether Hull should personally speak on the July 4th broadcast, pending confirmation that Japan's Foreign Minister will participate.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Dunn on Proposed Secretary of State Talk for July 4th Broadcast

subfiles.about: Reports the substitution of Prince Tokugawa for Foreign Minister Hirota and approves selecting non-official American speakers for the broadcast.
subfiles.from: James Clement Dunn, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Dunn notes Japan's Foreign Minister withdrew from the broadcast for Prince Tokugawa, so State will substitute a private American speaker.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Dunn on Substitution of Prince Tokugawa and Non-Official American Speakers
